title: Stream Runner: Difficulty as a Speed Curve, UI Reduced to Two Buttons
subtitle: A minimalist auto-runner case study: score equals distance, a one-obstacle-one-button mapping, and how a 0.6s dodge window keeps high speeds readable.

cover.alt: Stream Runner: Difficulty as a Speed Curve, UI Reduced to Two Buttons

coverWide.alt: Stream Runner: Difficulty as a Speed Curve, UI Reduced to Two Buttons

corePoints: Collection economy cut: score equals distance, so the speed curve is the only difficulty knob
Binary mapping: one obstacle type per button, failures are easy to attribute
Window 0.6s < interval floor 0.8s: you never face more than one obstacle at a time
Speed ramp stacked with shrinking intervals; gentle slopes make the first seconds a tutorial

breakdown.title: Rule Skeleton
bullets: Auto-run: base speed 10 units/s, ramping +0.5 per second linearly
Ground obstacles require SLIDE, air obstacles require JUMP; dodge window is 0.6s
Score equals distance (1 unit = 1 point, rounded at settlement); 3 lives, run ends on the third crash
High score is compared and updated at settlement; Play Again restarts instantly

breakdown.title: Behavior Loop
bullets: Tap Start Game in menu → data resets → core/runner.start
Read the obstacle type while auto-scrolling → press the matching button → dodge or lose 1 life
runner.finish → score/distance written back → result screen shows score and high score
A hands-off run lasts ~6 seconds for ~65 points: an ultra-short loop of about ten seconds per round

breakdown.title: Implementation Notes
bullets: core/runner carries all gameplay: five actions (start/jump/slide/setSpeed/reset) plus runner.crash and runner.finish events
Obstacle interval starts at 2s, shrinks 0.05 per second, floored at 0.8s — stacking with the speed curve into one pressure curve
All parameters are data-key driven (runnerSpeed/obstacleInterval/jumpDuration, etc.); tuning requires no code change
Known limitation: skin text {{key}} placeholders currently render literally, so HUD numbers do not tick
